children.text: Thermoelectric generators and refrigerators

Retain Joule, Seebeck and Peltier effects only, with temperature-independent coefficients. A thermocouple AB has emf α(T1−T2), junction Peltier heat πI and no heat exchange with surroundings except at reservoirs. Fourier heat current is q=−kS dT/dx. Both legs have length L and parameters ρA,ρB,kA,kB,SA,SB. Their series electrical resistance is \(R=L(\rho_A/S_A+\rho_B/S_B)\) and parallel thermal conductance is \(K=(k_AS_A+k_BS_B)/L\). Define Z=α²/(KR). For numerical work each material has resistivity \(1.0\times10^{-5}\) Ω m and conductivity 1.4 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, L=0.020 m and α=420 μV/K. Material A is Bi2Te2.7Se0.3 and B is Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3. In generator mode T1>T2. In refrigerator mode the current removes heat from the isolated upper junction at T1 and rejects it to the lower sink at T2, eventually T1<T2. Ignore radiation and convection.

children.text: Thermoelectric generators and refrigerators
a1.1. Temperature profile with Joule heating
Heat balance gives \(kS T^{\prime\prime}=-\rho I^2/S\). Integrate and impose both temperatures: \[T(x)=T_1+(T_2-T_1)x/L+\frac{\rho I^2}{2kS^2}x(L-x).\]
a1.2. Heat current along a leg
Differentiate A1.1: \(q=kS(T_1-T_2)/L+(\rho I^2/S)(x-L/2)\). With R=ρL/S and K=kS/L, \(q(0)=K(T_1-T_2)-RI^2/2\) and \(q(L)=K(T_1-T_2)+RI^2/2\). Half the Joule heat flows to each end.
a2.1. Reversible hot-side heat
By the Peltier definition, \(q_1=\pi_1I\).
a2.2. Reversible cold-side heat
\(q_2=\pi_2I\), with the positive quantities denoting received and rejected heat in the generator cycle.
a2.3. Reversible electrical power
\(P=\mathcal E I=\alpha(T_1-T_2)I\).
a2.4. Kelvin relation
The ideal efficiency is P/q1=(T1−T2)/T1. Substitute the preceding heat and power to obtain π1=αT1. At any junction \(\pi=\alpha T\).
a3.1. Generator heat balances
Add the conductive, Peltier and split Joule contributions: \[q_1=K(T_1-T_2)+\alpha T_1I-RI^2/2,\quad q_2=K(T_1-T_2)+\alpha T_2I+RI^2/2.\] Their difference is load power α(T1−T2)I−RI².
a3.2. Efficiency with a load
The circuit current is \(I=\alpha(T_1-T_2)/[R(1+m)]\). Divide I²RL by q1 to get \[\eta=\frac{m(T_1-T_2)}{(KR/\alpha^2)(1+m)^2+T_1(1+m)-(T_1-T_2)/2}.\]
a3.3. Figure-of-merit form
Substitute Z=α²/(KR): \[\eta=\eta_c\frac m{(1+m)^2/(ZT_1)+(1+m)-\eta_c/2}.\]
a4.1. Efficiency at maximum power

Power is proportional to m/(1+m)² and peaks at m=1. Substitution gives \[\eta_P=\frac{T_1-T_2}{4/Z+(3T_1+T_2)/2}.\] The source prints T1−T1 in one numerator, a typographical error corrected by its derivation.
a4.2. Load for maximum efficiency
Differentiate A3.3 with respect to m. The positive stationary root is \(M=\sqrt{1+Z(T_1+T_2)/2}\). It is larger than one for Z>0.
a4.3. Maximum generator efficiency
At m=M the efficiency simplifies to \[\eta_{max}=\frac{T_1-T_2}{T_1}\frac{M-1}{M+T_2/T_1},\qquad M=\sqrt{1+Z(T_1+T_2)/2}.\]
a5.1. Optimal leg-area ratio
Minimize KR=(kASA+kBSB)(ρA/SA+ρB/SB). Setting the derivative with respect to SB/SA to zero gives \(S_B/S_A=\sqrt{\rho_Bk_A/(\rho_Ak_B)}\).
a5.2. Best material figure of merit
The minimum product is \(KR=(\sqrt{\rho_Ak_A}+\sqrt{\rho_Bk_B})^2\), hence \[Z_m=\frac{\alpha^2}{(\sqrt{\rho_Ak_A}+\sqrt{\rho_Bk_B})^2}.\]
a6.1. Numerical efficiency at maximum power
The matched materials give Zm=α²/(4ρk)=0.00315 K⁻¹. With m=1, ηopt≈0.0586, or 5.86%. Using rounded Z=0.0032 gives the source's approximately 5.84% to 5.9%. Carnot is 120/423≈28.4%, so ηopt/ηc≈0.21.
a6.2. Numerical maximum efficiency
M=√(1+0.00315×363)≈1.46. The maximum efficiency is approximately 0.060, or 6.0%. It uses a different load from maximum power.
b1.1. Cooling power
The upper Peltier term removes heat while conduction from the warm sink and half the Joule heat oppose cooling: \[q_C=\alpha T_1I-K(T_2-T_1)-RI^2/2.\]
b1.2. Maximum temperature depression
At fixed temperatures qC is largest at I=αT1/R. Its zero at the minimum attainable temperature gives \(\Delta T_{max}=ZT_{1,min}^2/2\).
b2.1. Minimum cold temperature
The positive solution of ZmT1²/2+T1−T2=0 is \(T_{1,min}=[\sqrt{1+2Z_mT_2}-1]/Z_m\simeq222\,\mathrm K\).
b2.2. Working current at the limit
The pair resistance is R=2ρL/S=0.004 Ω. Thus \(I_w=\alpha T_{1,min}/R\simeq23.3\,\mathrm A\).
b3.1. Coefficient of performance
The required source power is \(P=\alpha(T_2-T_1)I+RI^2\). Therefore \[\beta=\frac{\alpha T_1I-K(T_2-T_1)-RI^2/2}{\alpha(T_2-T_1)I+RI^2}.\]
b3.2. Current for maximum COP
Let TM=(T1+T2)/2. Differentiate β and take the positive root: \[I_\beta=\frac{\alpha(T_2-T_1)}{R(\sqrt{1+ZT_M}-1)}.\] This differs from the maximum-cooling-power current.
b3.3. Maximum COP

With \(s=\sqrt{1+ZT_M}\), substitution gives \[\beta_{max}=\frac{T_1}{T_2-T_1}\frac{s-T_2/T_1}{s+1}.\] Positive cooling at the optimum requires s>T2/T1. This tends to the Carnot COP as Z tends to infinity.
